problemStatement.formal: For fixed k >= 2 and large n, let A(n,k) be the integers m with n <= m <= n^k that have a divisor d satisfying n < d < 2n. Ordered increasingly, how large can the maximum consecutive gap in A(n,k) be? In particular, is it bounded by a power of log n, with constants depending on k?
problemStatement.plain: Among numbers up to n^k that have a divisor just above n, are the gaps between consecutive such numbers only polylogarithmic?

Let $k\geq 2$ and $n$ be sufficiently large depending on $k$. Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots \}$ be the set of those integers in $[n,n^k]$ which have a divisor in $(n,2n)$. Estimate\[\max_{i} a_{i+1}-a_i.\]Is this $\leq (\log n)^{O(1)}$?



See also [446].
